bullets.text: Armed conflict erupted in the Duskany region of Ostravia on September 3, 2025, when Karvale Front units opened artillery fire across the Varn River, striking the city of Varenholm.
An estimated 30,000 people fled Varenholm and surrounding villages in the first 36 hours, with 18,600 refugees registered across the border in Lumeria at Mirefeld.

A mediated humanitarian pause enabled the evacuation of around 4,200 civilians from the Weavers Quarter, and by day four the front line had stabilized along the Varn River with shelling sharply reduced.
Karvale Front artillery opens fire across the Varn River; explosions reported on the northern edge of Varenholm.
Ostravia declares a state of emergency in the Duskany region; residents urged into shelters as air raid sirens sound repeatedly.
First casualty figures released: at least 3 civilians killed and 12 wounded in the initial shelling.
A shell strikes the eastern wing of Halloway General Hospital; IHCO condemns the strike and demands protection of medical facilities.
Duskany Thermal Power Station shuts down after shrapnel damage; the Alder Gate bridge over the Varn River is destroyed.
ODF repels a Karvale Front river-crossing attempt near Selkova; civilian toll rises to 8 dead and 41 wounded.
Lumeria opens the Mirefeld border crossing to Ostravian civilians without visa checks as columns of vehicles leave Varenholm.
Rescue teams pull five survivors, including two children, from a collapsed apartment block on Tanners Row.
Mediated talks produce agreement on a 3-hour humanitarian pause and an evacuation corridor via Corver Street.
The humanitarian corridor opens; despite a brief halt after shelling near the route, around 4,200 civilians are evacuated from the Weavers Quarter.
An IHCO convoy of 12 aid trucks crosses into Duskany from Lumeria; the pause arrangement is extended to daily 3-hour windows.
Day-four briefing: front line static along the Varn River, shelling incidents down 60 percent, power partially restored in central Varenholm.
At least 3 civilians were killed in the initial shelling of Varenholm.
The civilian death toll rose to 8 by the second day of fighting.
After four days, officials confirmed 14 civilian and 6 military deaths.
Twelve people were wounded in the opening bombardment, rising to 41 by the second day and 97 overall after four days.
Halloway General Hospital received the wounded and appealed for blood donors before itself being struck.
Two Ostravian Relief Society volunteers were lightly injured by shrapnel near the corridor route and were reported in stable condition.
At least 11 civilians were reported unaccounted for in Varenholm's northern districts, with families directed to the ORS hotline.
Seven of the missing were later located safe in shelters or in Lumeria, leaving 4 cases open at the end of the reporting window.
Residents were reported trapped in basements in the Weavers Quarter, including on Foundry Lane, where shelling was too heavy to leave.
People were trapped under two collapsed apartment buildings in Varenholm while rescue teams dug through the rubble.
Five survivors, including two children, were pulled from a collapsed apartment block on Tanners Row.
An elderly couple trapped for two days in a Foundry Lane basement were brought out during the corridor operation.
Seven previously unaccounted-for residents were found safe in shelters or across the border in Lumeria.
The eastern wing of Halloway General Hospital was struck and rendered unusable.
Shrapnel damaged the transformer yard of the Duskany Thermal Power Station, forcing a shutdown.
A city damage survey recorded at least 220 residential buildings damaged in the northern districts.
The bell tower of the Old Weavers Guild Hall, a 400-year-old landmark, was badly damaged by shelling.
A water pumping station and a mobile relay mast were damaged, disrupting utilities and communications.
The Alder Gate bridge over the Varn River was destroyed, severing the main road between Varenholm and Selkova.
Thirty-four residential buildings in Varenholm's northern districts were recorded as destroyed.
Rolling blackouts affected Varenholm after the power station shutdown.
Running water was limited to three hours a day after damage to a pumping station.
Mobile coverage failed across the northern districts after a relay mast was hit.
Fuel stations along evacuation route D4 ran dry, and pharmacies reported shortages of insulin and blood pressure medication.
Halloway General Hospital resumed emergency surgery in its west wing after generator deliveries.
Power was partially restored in central Varenholm after crews patched the transformer yard.
Southbound trains from Varenholm Central Station resumed on a reduced, free timetable for evacuees.
Residents were urged into shelters, with families using metro stations and basements during repeated air raid alerts.
A negotiated corridor via Corver Street evacuated around 4,200 civilians from the Weavers Quarter, including 60 hospital patients, with priority given to elderly, disabled and families with children.
ORS opened reception points at Varenholm Central Station and the Millgate school for residents fleeing the northern districts.
An estimated 30,000 people fled Varenholm and surrounding villages within the first 36 hours.
Lumerian authorities registered 18,600 Ostravian refugees at the Mirefeld crossing, doubling reception capacity with IHCO support.
School buildings in southern Varenholm sheltered about 5,500 internally displaced people.
As shelling eased, some shops reopened in the Brassmarket district and residents began queuing calmly for bread.
The primary hazard was sustained cross-river artillery shelling of populated districts of Varenholm by Karvale Front forces.
Ground fighting was concentrated along the Varn River, including a repelled crossing attempt near Selkova.
Strikes near the humanitarian corridor route during the agreed pause posed a direct risk to evacuees and aid workers.
ODF counter-battery strikes on artillery positions north of the river were credited with reducing shelling intensity by about 60 percent by day four.
The status of Selkova remained contested, with competing claims of control.
A wider intervention by the Northern Compact remained unconfirmed, with Compact officials describing their role as limited to mediation.
Ostravia declared a state of emergency in the Duskany region within hours of the first strikes.
Rescue teams conducted search operations at two collapsed apartment buildings, recovering multiple survivors.
Mediated negotiations produced a 3-hour humanitarian pause, later extended to daily windows, with buses staged at Varenholm Central Station under ORS escort.
Authorities urged residents to use SMS in the northern districts after mobile coverage failed.
The city council published a map of water distribution points and advised residents to check it before traveling.
Casualty and situation updates were issued by the regional governor, the ODF, the mayor and IHCO throughout the four days.
Fact-checkers debunked a viral video that used video game footage to claim Karvale Front tanks had entered central Varenholm.
Families of missing persons were directed to the ORS hotline 084.
Halloway General Hospital appealed for blood donors, and ORS asked donors to prioritize scarce medical supplies such as insulin.
Residents used social media to request evacuation of trapped relatives, including from Foundry Lane in the Weavers Quarter.
An IHCO convoy of 12 trucks delivered food, water and medical supplies to Duskany via the Mirefeld crossing.
Generator deliveries restored surgical capacity at Halloway General Hospital, and Lumerian volunteers provided hot food and blankets to arriving refugees.
Displaced residents received shelter in converted school buildings and services at ORS reception points.
Lumerian volunteers welcomed refugees at Mirefeld with hot soup and blankets.
Residents expressed fear during the bombardment alongside solidarity, with accounts of neighbors sheltering together and sharing music in metro stations.
Grief over damage to the Old Weavers Guild Hall landmark and pride in local volunteers were recurring themes.
